I'm Kath, a researcher working on real-time epidemiological analysis. 
I focus on quantitative modelling as a way of supporting public health decisions to control infectious disease outbreaks. 
I'm especially interested in model evaluation, comparison, and combination.
My work is openly available by default.

I work in the [Centre for Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Disease](https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/research/centres/centre-mathematical-modelling-infectious-diseases) in London, based in the [epiforecasts](https://epiforecasts.io/) group. 
I'm a happy Londoner, a feminist, and a [community gardener](https://www.albertatra.org/alberta-fruit-commons).


::: {.callout-note title="My work" collapse="true"}

I focus on using quantitative modelling to understand infectious disease dynamics, with specific experience in real-time forecasting. 
I'm particularly interested in evaluating evidence synthesis and expert advice in public health policy.

I aim to make all of my work openly available, from concept to code to publication. 
If you are interested in any of my work and can't find it, please contact me.
